::: {.book-summary} ## Book Summary Insight Ezekiel proclaims God's holiness, judgment, and future restoration through vivid visions and prophetic signs. The book teaches that God acts for the sake of His holy name and will restore His people. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 1
Ezekiel 1:28
The appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD
### Why This Verse Foundational vision of God's glory ### Chapter Insight This chapter records Ezekiel's vision of God's glory. The key verse reveals God's majesty and sovereignty even during exile. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 2
Ezekiel 2:6
Be not afraid of them
### Why This Verse Call to prophetic courage ### Chapter Insight This chapter contains Ezekiel's commission as a prophet. The key verse emphasizes faithful proclamation regardless of the people's response. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 3
Ezekiel 3:17
Son of man, I have made thee a watchman
### Why This Verse One of Ezekiel's defining verses ### Chapter Insight This chapter establishes Ezekiel as a watchman for Israel. The key verse highlights personal responsibility to warn others of God's truth. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 4
Ezekiel 4:6
I have appointed thee each day for a year
### Why This Verse Famous prophetic sign ### Chapter Insight This chapter uses symbolic acts to portray Jerusalem's coming siege. The key verse demonstrates the certainty of God's judgment. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 5
Ezekiel 5:8
I, even I, am against thee
### Why This Verse Judgment against Jerusalem ### Chapter Insight This chapter symbolizes the scattering of Jerusalem's inhabitants. The key verse emphasizes the consequences of persistent rebellion. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 6
Ezekiel 6:10
They shall know that I am the LORD
### Why This Verse Repeated theme in Ezekiel ### Chapter Insight This chapter prophesies against Israel's idolatrous high places. The key verse reveals God's desire that His people recognize Him as Lord. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 7
Ezekiel 7:19
Their silver and gold shall not deliver them
### Why This Verse Futility of wealth ### Chapter Insight This chapter announces the approaching end of judgment. The key verse emphasizes the inevitability of God's justice. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 8
Ezekiel 8:6
Great abominations
### Why This Verse Temple corruption exposed ### Chapter Insight This chapter reveals the hidden idolatry within the Temple. The key verse exposes the spiritual corruption that provoked God's judgment. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 9
Ezekiel 9:4
Set a mark upon the foreheads
### Why This Verse Protection of the faithful remnant ### Chapter Insight This chapter depicts judgment upon Jerusalem with protection for the faithful remnant. The key verse highlights God's distinction between the righteous and the wicked. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 10
Ezekiel 10:18
The glory of the LORD departed
### Why This Verse Major turning point ### Chapter Insight This chapter records the departure of God's glory from the Temple. The key verse symbolizes the seriousness of covenant unfaithfulness. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 11
Ezekiel 11:19
I will give them one heart and a new spirit
### Why This Verse Major restoration promise ### Chapter Insight This chapter promises future restoration despite present judgment. The key verse foretells God giving His people a new heart and spirit. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 12
Ezekiel 12:25
I am the LORD; I will speak
### Why This Verse Certainty of God's word ### Chapter Insight This chapter portrays exile through symbolic actions. The key verse demonstrates that God's warnings will surely come to pass. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 13
Ezekiel 13:10
They have seduced My people, saying, Peace
### Why This Verse False prophets condemned ### Chapter Insight This chapter condemns false prophets and false assurances. The key verse emphasizes the danger of proclaiming peace where God has not spoken. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 14
Ezekiel 14:14
Though Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it
### Why This Verse Individual responsibility emphasized ### Chapter Insight This chapter addresses idolatry within the heart. The key verse teaches that true repentance must be inward as well as outward. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 15
Ezekiel 15:6
As the vine among the trees
### Why This Verse Worthless vine metaphor ### Chapter Insight This chapter compares Jerusalem to a useless vine. The key verse illustrates the consequences of failing God's intended purpose. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 16
Ezekiel 16:60
I will remember My covenant with thee
### Why This Verse Grace despite unfaithfulness ### Chapter Insight This chapter portrays Jerusalem as an unfaithful spouse. The key verse highlights God's grace despite profound covenant betrayal. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 17
Ezekiel 17:24
I the LORD bring down the high tree
### Why This Verse God's sovereignty over nations ### Chapter Insight This chapter uses a parable of eagles and a vine. The key verse points to God's ultimate establishment of His kingdom. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 18
Ezekiel 18:20
The soul that sinneth, it shall die
### Why This Verse One of Ezekiel's most important theological statements ### Chapter Insight This chapter emphasizes individual responsibility before God. The key verse teaches that each person is accountable for his own choices. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 19
Ezekiel 19:10
Thy mother is like a vine
### Why This Verse Lament for Judah's rulers ### Chapter Insight This chapter laments the downfall of Judah's leaders. The key verse reflects the tragic consequences of failed leadership. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 20
Ezekiel 20:12
I gave them My Sabbaths
### Why This Verse Covenant sign emphasized ### Chapter Insight This chapter reviews Israel's history of rebellion. The key verse highlights God's faithfulness despite continual disobedience. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 21
Ezekiel 21:27
Until He come whose right it is
### Why This Verse Frequently viewed as messianic ### Chapter Insight This chapter announces the sword of God's judgment. The key verse emphasizes the certainty of coming punishment. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 22
Ezekiel 22:30
I sought for a man among them
### Why This Verse One of the most quoted verses in Ezekiel ### Chapter Insight This chapter catalogs Jerusalem's sins. The key verse reveals God's search for someone to stand in the gap for the nation. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 23
Ezekiel 23:49
Ye shall know that I am the Lord GOD
### Why This Verse Judgment and recognition ### Chapter Insight This chapter uses two sisters to depict Israel's and Judah's unfaithfulness. The key verse demonstrates the seriousness of spiritual adultery. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 24
Ezekiel 24:16
I take away from thee the desire of thine eyes
### Why This Verse Profound prophetic sign ### Chapter Insight This chapter marks the beginning of Jerusalem's final siege. The key verse symbolizes God's judgment through the image of a boiling pot. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 25
Ezekiel 25:17
They shall know that I am the LORD
### Why This Verse Famous judgment formula ### Chapter Insight This chapter pronounces judgment on Israel's neighboring nations. The key verse demonstrates that God holds all nations accountable for their actions. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 26
Ezekiel 26:14
Thou shalt be built no more
### Why This Verse Prophecy against Tyre ### Chapter Insight This chapter prophesies the fall of Tyre. The key verse reveals God's sovereignty over powerful cities and empires. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 27
Ezekiel 27:3
O Tyre, thou hast said, I am of perfect beauty
### Why This Verse Beginning of Tyre's lament ### Chapter Insight This chapter laments the downfall of Tyre's commercial greatness. The key verse highlights the fragility of wealth and worldly success. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 28
Ezekiel 28:17
Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty
### Why This Verse Often cited regarding pride and downfall ### Chapter Insight This chapter condemns the pride of Tyre's ruler. The key verse warns that self-exaltation leads to destruction. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 29
Ezekiel 29:3
I am against thee, Pharaoh
### Why This Verse Judgment on Egypt ### Chapter Insight This chapter announces judgment against Egypt. The key verse demonstrates the futility of trusting human power instead of God. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 30
Ezekiel 30:3
The day of the LORD is near
### Why This Verse Major prophetic theme ### Chapter Insight This chapter continues the prophecy against Egypt. The key verse emphasizes God's authority over nations and rulers. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 31
Ezekiel 31:10
Because thou hast lifted up thyself in height
### Why This Verse Pride preceding judgment ### Chapter Insight This chapter compares Egypt to a great tree brought low. The key verse illustrates the downfall of pride before God. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 32
Ezekiel 32:7
I will cover the heavens and make the stars dark
### Why This Verse Cosmic judgment imagery ### Chapter Insight This chapter laments Pharaoh and Egypt's coming judgment. The key verse reminds nations that earthly glory is temporary. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 33
Ezekiel 33:11
I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked
### Why This Verse One of Ezekiel's central themes ### Chapter Insight This chapter renews Ezekiel's commission as a watchman. The key verse emphasizes personal responsibility in responding to God's warnings. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 34
Ezekiel 34:16
I will seek that which was lost
### Why This Verse Shepherd imagery later echoed by Jesus ### Chapter Insight This chapter condemns Israel's false shepherds and promises God's care. The key verse points to the coming Shepherd-King who will tend His flock. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 35
Ezekiel 35:15
As thou didst rejoice over the inheritance of Israel
### Why This Verse Judgment on Edom ### Chapter Insight This chapter prophesies judgment against Edom. The key verse highlights God's justice toward those who oppose His people. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 36
Ezekiel 36:26
A new heart also will I give you
### Why This Verse One of the most important restoration promises ### Chapter Insight This chapter promises Israel's restoration and spiritual renewal. The key verse foretells God giving His people a new heart and spirit. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 37
Ezekiel 37:5
I will cause breath to enter into you
### Why This Verse Famous valley of dry bones prophecy ### Chapter Insight This chapter contains the vision of the Valley of Dry Bones. The key verse demonstrates God's power to bring life, restoration, and hope from apparent impossibility. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 38
Ezekiel 38:23
Thus will I magnify Myself
### Why This Verse God's victory over Gog ### Chapter Insight This chapter introduces the prophecy concerning Gog. The key verse emphasizes God's ultimate victory over hostile nations. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 39
Ezekiel 39:29
I have poured out My Spirit
### Why This Verse Restoration and renewal ### Chapter Insight This chapter continues God's judgment against Gog. The key verse reveals God's purpose of making His holiness known among the nations. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 40
Ezekiel 40:4
Declare all that thou seest
### Why This Verse Vision of the future temple ### Chapter Insight This chapter begins the vision of the future Temple. The key verse emphasizes God's orderly and holy design for worship. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 41
Ezekiel 41:4
This is the most holy place
### Why This Verse Temple centerpiece ### Chapter Insight This chapter details the structure of the Temple. The key verse highlights the centrality of God's dwelling place. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 42
Ezekiel 42:20
To make a separation between holy and common
### Why This Verse Temple holiness ### Chapter Insight This chapter describes the Temple chambers and sacred spaces. The key verse emphasizes holiness and separation unto God. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 43
Ezekiel 43:2
The glory of the God of Israel came
### Why This Verse Return of God's glory ### Chapter Insight This chapter records the return of God's glory to the Temple. The key verse marks the restoration of God's presence among His people. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 44
Ezekiel 44:23
Teach My people the difference between holy and profane
### Why This Verse Priestly responsibility ### Chapter Insight This chapter establishes regulations for worship and priestly service. The key verse emphasizes reverence and holiness in approaching God. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 45
Ezekiel 45:9
Remove violence and spoil
### Why This Verse Call to justice ### Chapter Insight This chapter outlines sacred portions of land and worship practices. The key verse highlights justice and proper stewardship. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 46
Ezekiel 46:9
None shall return by the way he came
### Why This Verse Worship order ### Chapter Insight This chapter describes offerings and worship observances. The key verse emphasizes regular devotion and obedience. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 47
Ezekiel 47:9
Everything shall live where the river comes
### Why This Verse River of life vision ### Chapter Insight This chapter contains the vision of the river flowing from the Temple. The key verse portrays God's life-giving blessing flowing outward to bring healing. ::: ::: {.chapter-entry} ## Chapter 48
Ezekiel 48:35
The LORD is there
### Why This Verse Final message of Ezekiel (Jehovah-Shammah) ### Chapter Insight This chapter concludes with the division of the land and the new city. The key verse declares the city's name: "The LORD Is There." :::
